title: NeuroSYNC submits parliamentary evidence on low-energy computing priorities
summary: On 2026-05-14, the UK Multidisciplinary Centre for Neuromorphic Systems and Computing (NeuroSYNC) submitted written evidence to the UK Parliament's Science, Innovation and Technology Committee regarding Low-Energy Computing. The submission outlines how neuromorphic computing addresses AI energy demands while strengthening UK leadership in next-generation technologies. Based on stakeholder surveys and roadmapping workshops, NeuroSYNC identified three priorities: developing shared national testbed infrastructure for neuromorphic hardware; investing in open software tools and benchmarking standards; and supporting long-term application-driven collaboration between academia, industry, and government.
tldr: NeuroSYNC submitted parliamentary evidence outlining key priorities to advance the UK's neuromorphic computing ecosystem via shared infrastructure, open tools, and cross-sector collaboration.
